author: Temminck, 1829
habitat: 서해 섬과 해안의 트인 맨땅, 풀밭, 밭
summary: 2003년 5월 대흑산도에서 처음 기록된 길잃은새로, 서해 섬과 해안에서 봄(4–5월)에 몇 차례 기록되었고 가을(10월)에도 관찰 기록이 있다. 그리스 북부와 남러시아에서 중앙아시아를 거쳐 중국 동북부까지 반사막과 건조한 초원에서 번식하고, 아프리카 동북부와 아라비아반도, 인도 중부에서 겨울을 난다. 땅 위를 재빨리 달리다 멈춰 몸을 꾸벅이며 딱정벌레 같은 곤충을 잡고, 흙더미 위에 곧게 서서 주위를 살핀다.

young: 어린새는 어른새와 비슷하나 윗면에 담황색 기와 희미한 줄무늬가 있고, 가슴에 잔 갈색 얼룩이 있으며 날개깃 가장자리가 담황색이다. 첫 겨울에는 어른새와 같아진다.

art.subject: Isabelline Wheatear (Oenanthe isabellina), adult (sexes nearly alike) as a spring migrant on a Korean offshore island: whole upperparts plain pale sandy grey-brown, crown and back the same tone; a short, broad creamy-white supercilium, brightest in front of the eye; lores blackish in the male, brownish in the female; wings pale sandy-brown with buff-fringed coverts and tertials, the small black alula standing out as a dark spot at the bend of the wing; throat whitish, breast warm buff, belly and undertail coverts creamy white; rump and uppertail coverts white; tail white at the base with a broad black terminal band and only a short black centre. Bill black, fairly long and strong for a wheatear; eye dark; legs long and black.
art.pose: standing very upright on a low rock with the tail slightly lowered, side view
art.scene: short-grazed turf and bare sandy ground near the shore of a Korean offshore island during spring migration (April–May), bright clear light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view standing very upright on a low rock: large, big-headed wheatear, plain pale sandy upperparts, creamy-white supercilium broadest in front of the eye, fairly long, strong bill, pale sandy wings with a small isolated black alula at the bend of the wing, buff breast, creamy-white belly, white rump, long black legs

adult, in flight seen squarely from above: head, body and tail in one line, wings spread straight out to the sides to their full span, pale sandy upperwing with dark-tipped primaries, sandy back, white rump, white tail with a broad black terminal band and black central feathers forming an inverted T
art.build: A large, pale wheatear, clearly bigger than a sparrow and slightly larger, bigger-headed and longer-legged than Northern Wheatear; stands very upright, often bobs and runs fast over bare ground. Bill black, straight and strong, shorter than the head. Legs long and black with much of the tarsus visible. At rest the wingtips fall well short of the tail tip, so the tail looks rather short. In flight the wings look pale with whitish underwing coverts, the white rump contrasts with the broad black tail band. Tail square-ended.
avoid: Do not paint a black throat or black face — that is male Desert Wheatear; Isabelline has only dark lores on a pale face.
Do not paint a blue-grey back, black wings or a black eye mask; those belong to breeding male Northern Wheatear.
Do not make the wings dark brown or black; Isabelline wings are pale sandy, with only the small alula black.
Do not paint a nearly all-black tail (Desert Wheatear); Isabelline shows a white tail base and a broad black terminal band.
